ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: “Bring the mind here” is Bodhidharma’s demand when Huike asks him to settle his unquiet mind. Huike answers that after searching he cannot find it; Bodhidharma replies that he has settled it. Later masters repeatedly raise the entire exchange, while Miyun Yuanwu reuses the wording directly when a student claims to have a mind.
EvidenceBody: The fixed case has Huike ask for his mind to be settled. Bodhidharma says, “bring the mind here and I will settle it for you”; Huike reports that the mind cannot be found, and Bodhidharma closes the exchange.
Dahui Zonggao preserves the demand inside an extended public explanation of Huike’s search through the received teachings and categories before reporting that no body of mind can be found.
Juelang Daosheng raises the case critically and says that both the old exchange and his own comment deserve blows; the inherited wording remains the object of public testing.
Miyun Yuanwu tells his own student, “since you have a mind, bring the mind here,” and receives a verse in reply. This is a fresh direct deployment, not merely containment in the Bodhidharma case.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A plain imperative becomes the opening demand of the public mind-settling case and is reusable as a direct challenge to someone who claims to possess a mind.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The demand does not define mind as an object that the entry can supply; the case records Huike’s failure to find one.

ComparedThings: Bodhidharma’s demand and Miyun’s reuse are the same imperative to bring forth the claimed mind
DifferentThingTest.Reason: Bodhidharma’s demand and Miyun’s reuse are the same imperative to bring forth the claimed mind. Quotation versus fresh address changes the occasion, not the action requested.

DraftEvidence.AliasRationale: Bring, mind, me, here, and forth cover natural English word order for the imperative; ‘settle the mind’ belongs to the surrounding 安心 exchange, not the headword itself.

ModifierControls.reason: 把將心來 is Miyun’s expanded imperative and was retained as a deployment; bare 將心 in unrelated constructions was excluded.

FamilyControls.reason: 安心, 覓心了不可得, and 與汝安心竟 form the rest of the Bodhidharma–Huike case but are not alternate translations of 將心來.
